cases.rationale: Both cohorts carry D3163-01R23 receipts for rigid-plastic single-lap apparent shear.
Both cohorts carry D5868-01R23 receipts for FRP-to-FRP single-lap apparent shear.
A wettability observation cannot supply an apparent-shear transfer endpoint.
A lap-shear measurement cannot be promoted to a service-lifetime claim.
The older reaffirmation is not the active D3163-01R23 registry entry.
D3163 is not the metal-to-metal lap-shear method.
D5868 is registered for single-lap FRP joints, not double-lap.
The baseline method receipt lacks a well-formed protocol digest.
The bridge cohort identities must exactly match each method receipt.
The same specimen cannot be counted in both baseline and candidate cohorts.
Every required endpoint must have a method-qualified bridge receipt.
A single observation receipt cannot represent both independent cohorts.
Baseline and candidate comparisons must use the same test protocol revision and digest.
A receipt for apparent shear cannot be reused to claim a different failure-mode endpoint.
D5868 covers both FRP-to-FRP and FRP-to-metal, but the same standard family does not establish equivalence between two different adherend pair classes.
